candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is spindle cell lipoma (SCL) with focal intramuscular involvement, characterized by bland spindle cells, mature adipocytes, and thickened collagen bundles on pathology. Fibrolipomatous hamartoma is a separate entity classically associated with peripheral nerve enlargement and fibrofatty infiltration around nerve fascicles. While both involve fibrous and fatty tissue, fibrolipomatous hamartoma asserts an incompatible subtype and etiology relative to SCL. The histologic findings (subcutaneous spindle cell proliferation with bland cytomorphology, fragmented collagen, and intramuscular extension) are characteristic of SCL, not fibrolipomatous hamartoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma is a distinct entity (typically involving peripheral nerves with fibrofatty proliferation) and does not map to spindle cell lipoma; both involve adipose and fibrous tissue but represent incompatible diagnostic subtypes

case_quality_flags: Spindle cell lipoma in the facial region is an unusual anatomic location; prior nondiagnostic biopsies and misinterpretation as sebaceous hyperplasia noted as diagnostic challenge
